text:
How long must I shake my bells

And kiss your forehead, sad caricature?

To hit the target, of mystical virtue,

How many arrows must my quiver waste?


In the subtlest feints we will spend our soul,

And more than one frame we must destroy,

Before contemplating the finished Creature

Whose infernal desire fills us with sobs.


There are some who never knew their idol,

Accursed sculptors marked by opprobrium,

Who beat with fury upon breast and brow,


With no more than one hope, dark Capitol!

That Death, hovering like a renewed sun,

Will finally make the flowers of their mind burst open.

translation.title: The Death of Artists
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the artist's exhausting search for the finished creature and death as the final flowering.
